title: Vedanta Iron and Steel reports Rs 122 crore net profit in Q1
description: Vedanta Iron and Steel Ltd posted a Rs 122 crore net profit for the June quarter. This marks a significant turnaround from the Rs 142 crore net loss incurred last year. The company's revenue from operations increased to Rs 3,662 crore during this period. These earnings represent the first results after its demerger from Vedanta Ltd. The company operates integrated steel and mining assets across key mineral belts.

title: Vedanta Power Q1 Results: Company logs quarterly loss of Rs 449 crore
description: Vedanta Power has posted a standalone loss of Rs 449 crore for the June quarter, albeit with total income rising to Rs 1,844 crore in the first fiscal quarter. Power sales saw a significant boost of 38 percent year-on-year, attributed to improved generation from essential assets. The company envisions expanding its capacity to 20 GW by FY33, aiming to rank among the top three private power sector players.

title: US Stocks: US market opens lower ahead of Fed decision; chip stocks wobble
description: Major stock indexes on Wall Street opened lower on Wednesday. Investors awaited the Federal Reserve's monetary policy decision amid Middle East tensions. Chip stocks also faced pressure ahead of Big Tech earnings later this week. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 73.1 points at the open. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite also saw declines.

title: Karnataka Bank Q1 profit jumps 43% as asset quality improves
description: Karnataka Bank reported a 43% year-on-year rise in Q1 net profit to Rs 419 crore, driven by stronger business growth, improved asset quality and lower provisions. Net interest income, operating profit and margins increased, while advances and deposits posted healthy year-on-year growth.

title: Copper slips ahead of Fed rate decision, aluminium rises on Gulf fighting
description: Copper prices faced a downturn due to cautious trading leading up to the Federal Reserve's imminent interest rate decision. The easing of supply constraints in China added further downward pressure on both copper and zinc. Conversely, aluminium experienced an uptick as escalating conflicts in the Middle East raised supply concerns.

title: US Treasury yields rise after three-day fall as oil jumps, Fed decision looms
description: As oil prices surged, treasury yields took notice, raising inflation worries in the market. Traders are keeping a watchful eye on the Federal Reserve's expected decision to maintain interest rates today. Nonetheless, traders are fully anticipating a hike in September, with a solid possibility of another increase before the year's end.

title: Euro zone bonds snap three-day rally, yields rise with oil
description: As oil prices surged on Wednesday, Euro zone government bonds experienced a decline. Heightened hostilities in the Middle East were a major factor driving Brent crude upward. Economists are keenly observing energy trends for signs of inflation that might influence monetary policy changes, contributing to traders’ nervousness surrounding the upcoming interest rate announcement from the US Federal Reserve.

title: India bonds slip as oil prices hurt; Fed verdict in focus
description: On Wednesday, Indian government bonds took a hit due to renewed U.S. airstrikes in the Middle East, escalating tensions in the Gulf region. This escalation has led to a spike in oil prices and increased U.S. Treasury yields. The rising crude prices pose challenges for India's inflation, fiscal health, and current account. Investors can expect high global yields to continue, limiting the potential for rallies in Indian fixed income markets.

title: Cognizant forecasts weak quarterly revenue amid cautious client spending
description: Cognizant Technology has revised its third-quarter revenue projections, now falling short of Wall Street's expectations. The cautious stance of clients regarding discretionary IT expenditures and significant investments is evident. With AI adoption gaining momentum, enterprises are focusing more on data center infrastructures than software.
